traceability.evidence: Story file docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md defines requirements REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS, REQ-FLAT-CONFIG, REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS, REQ-RULE-OPTIONS, REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION, REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION and acceptance criteria including presets, ESLint v9 flat config usage, integration, documentation, and error handling.,Core preset implementation in src/index.ts: - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES defines flat rule severity map for all traceability rules. - createTraceabilityFlatConfig() returns a flat-config object `{ rules: { ...TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES } }` with fully-qualified rule IDs (e.g. "traceability/require-story-annotation"). - configs is defined as `{ recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()] }` and attached to the exported plugin. This matches REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS (recommended and strict presets as arrays) and REQ-FLAT-CONFIG (ESLint v9 flat config format).,Preset wiring and rule-severity correctness verified by tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts: - Confirms `plugin.configs === configs` and rules object names are as expected. - Asserts `configs.recommended[0].rules` contains required rules with correct severities (all core rules as "error" and valid-annotation-format as "warn"). - Asserts `configs.strict[0].rules` equals `configs.recommended[0].rules`. These tests passed in the Jest run, demonstrating correct preset content and consistent recommended/strict behavior.,Flat-config integration with ESLint v9 verified in tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts: - JSDoc header: `@supports docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS REQ-FLAT-CONFIG REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION`. - Uses `FlatESLint` from `eslint/use-at-your-own-risk` with `overrideConfig` set to `[baseConfig, ...configs.recommended]` / `[baseConfig, ...configs.strict]`, where `baseConfig` registers the plugin via `plugins: { traceability: traceabilityPlugin }`. - Lints simple JS code and asserts reported rule IDs include `"traceability/require-story-annotation"` for both recommended and strict presets. These tests passed, providing concrete evidence for REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS, REQ-FLAT-CONFIG, and REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION (composition with other configs and correct plugin registration pattern).,Rule option schema and config validation for rule options covered by tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts and tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts: - eslint-config-validation.test.ts (annotated with @supports REQ-RULE-OPTIONS and REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION) verifies `validStoryReference.meta.schema[0].properties` includes `storyDirectories`, `allowAbsolutePaths`, and `requireStoryExtension`, and `additionalProperties === false` (unknown options rejected by ESLint schema). - require-story-annotation-config.test.ts verifies `requireStoryAnnotation.meta.schema[0].properties` includes `scope` and `exportPriority`, and `additionalProperties === false`. These demonstrate rule-level configuration schemas and validation, satisfying REQ-RULE-OPTIONS and contributing to REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION.,Customizable story locations and path patterns implemented and documented: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts meta.schema (lines ~300–360) defines options `storyDirectories` (string[]), `allowAbsolutePaths` (boolean), `requireStoryExtension` (boolean), with `additionalProperties: false`. The rule uses these options at runtime to resolve and constrain story paths. - user-docs/api-reference.md documents valid-story-reference options under "traceability/valid-story-reference": `storyDirectories`, `allowAbsolutePaths`, `requireStoryExtension`, with example configuration, fulfilling REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS (custom directories and extension behavior) and REQ-RULE-OPTIONS.,Additional pattern-based customization and config error handling implemented in valid-annotation-format rule and tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts: - The rule supports nested `story.pattern` / `req.pattern` and flat `storyPathPattern` / `requirementIdPattern` options with example messages, as documented in user-docs/api-reference.md. - Tests include cases named "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES]" and several "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK...]" that verify: - Invalid regex patterns for options cause an `invalidRuleConfiguration` diagnostic with a detailed `details` field (e.g., `Invalid regular expression for option "storyPathPattern": "[unclosed"`). - The rule gracefully falls back to defaults and still validates annotations, emitting normal format errors alongside the configuration error. This demonstrates graceful handling of invalid rule configuration options and helpful diagnostics, addressing the story’s "Error Handling" acceptance criterion and REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION.,Integration and presets usage patterns for common project types provided in user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md and README.md: - ESLint 9 Setup Guide shows recommended/strict preset usage in flat configs and emphasizes the pattern: - Register plugin first: `{ plugins: { traceability } }`, then spread `...traceability.configs.recommended` or `...traceability.configs.strict`, explicitly mirroring REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS’ intent. - The guide contains sections and full examples for: - JavaScript-only projects, TypeScript projects, mixed JS/TS projects, test files, Node.js CJS config files, and monorepos, demonstrating REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION and the "User Experience" acceptance criterion for clear documentation for common project types. - It has a "Troubleshooting ESLint Configuration" section and multiple "Common Issues and Solutions" (e.g., parser misconfig, eslint:recommended usage, CLI flags, globals), supporting the "Documentation" acceptance criterion for configuration examples and troubleshooting. - README.md provides quick-start flat config examples, including combined use of `@eslint/js` and `traceability.configs.recommended`, and points to the ESLint 9 Setup Guide and API Reference for details.,Error handling and validation of configuration options are also supported via JSON Schema for options-heavy rules: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts meta.schema ensures type safety and disallows extra properties; tests in tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts confirm this. - For invalid pattern configuration in valid-annotation-format, tests assert an `invalidRuleConfiguration` messageId plus a clear `details` string, and that the rule still functions using defaults.
